products.title: Clay Curious: Sunday September 20th, 6:30pm - 8:30pm
products.body_html:
Curious about the pottery wheel? Come see what the buzz is all about in this fun, beginner-friendly session!

In just two hours, you'll get hands-on experience with the wheel, learning how to center clay, shape an open form, and pull up the walls to create your very own cup or bowl. Our friendly instructor will kick things off with a demo, then guide you step by step as you try it yourself.

At the end of class, you’ll choose your favorite piece to keep—we’ll handle the glazing and firing for you! Your finished piece will be ready for pickup in about three weeks, all included in the class price.

If you fall in love with the process (and we think you will!), check out our 8-week courses or join us for another Clay Curious session.

This class is for students age 18 and older. Price is per person. Refunds are limited; please read our refund policy for more information. We no longer provide refunds for COVID-19.

Note this is an evening class from 6:30-8:30pm

products.title: Fall Advanced Wheel: Thursday Evenings, 6:30pm - 9:30pm, September 10th - October 29th
products.body_html:
Are you ready to level up your pottery-wheel game? Our Advanced Wheel class might be a perfect next step for you!

Students must have at least 16 weeks of recent prior pottery wheel classes and be able to competently center two-three pounds of clay to register for this class.

Each session of our advanced classes has a different curriculum, but each class is centered around strengthening these core skills:

  • Consistency
  • Height
  • Weight
  • Glaze Chemistry
  • Alteration

Whether you are looking to throw larger work or learn specific advanced techniques, our advanced wheel class is designed to help each individual student achieve those goals.

Students who are enrolled in our 8-week classes also get free access to the studio during designated Open Studio times: come in and practice your throwing!

And the fine print:

  • Our beautiful studio has just about everything you need, except for a simple set of pottery tools. Bring your own or purchase a simple kit from us on the first day of class.
  • The first bag of clay is included in your class, after that each bag is sold separately.
  • While we highly recommend that you attend all sessions in a series in order to get the most out of the class, we also understand that you may need to miss a class. If this is your first time at our studio, please make sure you are able to attend your first class date.
  • This class is for advanced students.

products.title: Fall Beginner Wheel: Wednesday Evenings, 6:30pm - 9:30pm, September 9th - October 28th
products.body_html:
Have you always dreamed of throwing on the potter’s wheel? Our 8-week class is the perfect introduction to making your own functional pottery!

Our friendly, experienced instructors create a supportive atmosphere that encourages exploration and skill-building at your own pace. Through the course you’ll learn these essential techniques: 

  • making basic forms like cups and bowls
  • trimming your thrown pottery
  • how to make and attach handles
  • surface decoration and glazing

Students who are enrolled in our 8-week classes also get access to the studio during designated Open Studio times: come in and practice your throwing!

At the end of this 8-week class, you’ll come away with a new-found appreciation for this ancient art form, confidence in your new skills... and your very own handmade pottery!

And the fine print: 

  • While this class is geared towards beginners, everyone is welcome.
  • Our beautiful studio has just about everything you need, except for a simple set of pottery tools. Bring your own or purchase one of pottery essentials sets available at the studio on your first day of class.
  • One bag of clay is included as part of your tuition. Any clay after that, will be $20 per bag.
  • While we highly recommend that you attend all sessions in a series in order to get the most out of the class, we also understand that you may need to miss a class. If this is your first time at our studio, please make sure you are able to attend your first class date.

products.title: Making Monsters with Eva Funderburgh, Three Day Workshop Jan 29th - 31st, 1pm - 5pm
products.body_html:
Eva Funderburgh is back at Saltstone with another workshop! Eva is a Seattle-based artist known for her emotive animal forms and unique imaginary creatures. Especially in her technical skill in handbuilding and refining her beasts!

In this 3-day workshop, you will learn her techniques for building her sculptures and make your own pair of monsters. The workshop will cover using multiple pinch pots to build creatures, along with tips for capturing move and emotion within your form.

Workshop will be in-person hosted at Saltstone Ceramics in the Wallingford Neighborhood of Seattle.

This workshop is appropriate for all levels of experience with clay and is open to students 18 and older.

Eva Funderburgh is a Seattle-based sculptor working in ceramic, bronze, and installation.  Born in Seattle, she grew up in Kansas before moving to Pittsburgh at age 16. She attended Carnegie Mellon University, where she received a Bachelor’s of Science and Art. In 2010, she was an artist in residence in Denmark at the Guldagergaard International Ceramic Research Center, an experience that inspired her to revisit her college installation work.  In 2015, she was part of the Seattle’s Office of Arts and Culture Public Art Boot Camp. She now teaches bronze casting part time at Pratt Fine Art Center, and is a full time sculptor working in public art, installation, ceramics, and cast bronze. 

Note Eva Funderburgh's work is fired in a way our studio cannot accommodate.  Students can have the option of having Saltstone do a cone 6 clear, or taking the bisque ware home for atmospheric firing elsewhere.

The materials will be provided on-site. All firing services are included in the cost, and instructor will glaze your pieces in a clear for you.

Workshop registration is time/class-specific and is non-refundable. We no longer provide refunds for COVID-19. If you can't attend your workshop, we encourage you to give your spot to a friend.

If giving as a gift, please provide the contact information for the recipient in the purchase form.

products.title: Throwing Large Dinnerware Sets: 2 Week Intensive. August 17th - August 27th from 6:30 PM - 9:30 PM
products.body_html:
Looking to deepen your skills in a short but focused format? Join us this August for a 2 week, 4 session pottery intensive designed for dedicated makers who want to work on throwing larger and make a beautiful dinnerware set. At the end of the intensive, students should leave with 2 plates, 2 bowls, and 2 cups!

This accelerated course will meet twice a week for two weeks, with each class running 3 hours. Students should come prepared with prior wheel experience and the ability to center at least three pounds of clay.

What to Expect:
Day 1: Introduction to Project 8/17
Planning our your dinnerware set, with a focus on centering large and maintaining consistent, even walls. 

Day 2: Project continuation 8/20
Demo #2 and continuation of project.

Day 3: Trimming & Finishing Touches 8/24
Focus on trimming techniques, foot styles, and surface preparation.

Day 4: Glazing 8/27
Wrap up with glaze demos and application techniques to highlight your work. Learn strategies for layering, and finishing your work as well as glazing large work.

By the end of this intensive, you should walk away with experience in throwing large and refined your skills in consistency.

And the fine print:

  • While this class is geared towards intermediate students, everyone is welcome.
  • Our beautiful studio has just about everything you need, except for a simple set of pottery tools. Bring your own or purchase a simple kit from us on the first day of class.
  • The first bag of clay is included in your class, after that each bag is sold separately.
  • We highly recommend that you attend all sessions in a series in order to get the most out of the class.
  • Open studio access during gallery hours.

products.title: Kid's Clay Camp, Aug 17th - 21st, 9am - 12pm
products.body_html:
Kids’ Clay Camps are a fun way for kids to explore their creativity and learn some new skills in a collaborative, small group environment.  Kid's Clay Camp is for ages 6-12 years. All camps are 9am – 12pm. Each day will feature a group activity and time for individual making and decorating with ample instructor support. Projects can include slab mugs, clay pizza and toppings, pinch pot creatures, texture soap dishes, desert island sculptures, and more!

Class takes place at our Wallingford studio from 9am to 12pm everyday for a week. We recommend that students attend all sessions — there will not be make up sessions available.

Come join the fun!

Please read our refund policy before registering.

products.body_html:
Finally! A summer clay camp just for youth ages 12-17!

Whether you’re a brand new beginner or have lots of experience, you are sure to build skills in this class. Students will learn wheel-throwing and hand-building as well as techniques for finishing and glazing them. All materials are provided.

Are you interested in getting your hands muddy and learning the basics of wheel thrown pottery? This camp will offer teens a great opportunity to practice creating their own 3D works of art on the pottery wheel. The pottery wheel is a great way for youth to use art as a way to express themselves.

This whole-body creative effort will give your teen an engaging and exciting new skill that will keep them occupied for the week. With only ten students in the class, everyone is sure to get a lot of individual instruction.

Class takes place at our Wallingford studio from 9am to 12pm everyday for a week. We recommend that students attend all sessions — there will not be make up sessions available.

Come join the fun!

Please read our refund policy before registering.

products.title: BIPOC Wheel Night Sunday, October 4th, 6:30-8:30pm
products.body_html:
Our Clay Curious session is a great opportunity for people to try the potter's wheel for the first time and see what all the excitement is all about while being in a space that is safe and encouraging to beginners.

In this two hour session, our friendly instructor Jem Tong will give you a demonstration of how to throw and then guide you through the process of trying it out for yourself. You’ll learn how to center clay on the wheel, create an open form, and raise up the sides to a make beautiful cup or bowl with your own hands.

Each student will get to keep one piece of their choice. We will do all the firing and glazing for you and notify you once they are ready for pick up (usually takes one month).

This class is recommended for students age 18 and older, and for anyone who identifies as BIPOC.

Note that this is an evening class, from 6:30pm to 8:30pm.
